items.notes: Closes W-261105-02. Tally from sources familiar, per CBS.
items.text: House Republicans chose Jim Jordan over Steve Scalise, 106–73, as their leader for the next Congress, when they will be in the minority. Speaker Johnson is stepping aside; he says he stays in charge until early January.

The House voted 211–204 to send Rep. Massie’s articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Hegseth (over the Iran war) to committee, which in effect ends the effort in this Congress. Democrats, who take the majority in January, promise investigations; it is unclear whether they will try impeachment again.

The House aviation subcommittee cancelled its Nov 10 hearing with FAA Administrator Bedford on the $12.5bn air-traffic-control rollout and the FAA’s request for $30bn more, less than 24 hours beforehand. No reason or new date was given.

items.notes: Closes W-261107-03. Source gives conflicting totals (10,910 vs 10,772). Check CDC Federal Register notice.
items.text: CDC figures (as of Nov 6) put the DR Congo Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak at about 10,900 confirmed cases and 5,200 deaths, the second-largest on record, with cases now in Kenya and Nigeria. Since Nov 3 all international passengers to the US must attest they were not in DRC in the past 21 days; CDC rates US risk as low.

items.notes: Check BLS release for exact figures. AAA petrol average fell below $4/gal.
items.text: October consumer prices rose 0.4% (core 0.3%), above the 0.3% expected; no annual rate was published because October 2025 data were lost in the shutdown. Stocks fell (S&P 500 −0.4%, Nasdaq −0.7%, Dow −0.3%) and Nvidia dropped about 5.5%. Fed Governor Waller said a half-point December hike should be considered if core inflation runs at 0.3% or more.

items.notes: Case 26A560, Mullin v. Friends of the Ruidosa Church.
items.text: In an unsigned order, the Supreme Court lifted a district-court injunction so border wall and road construction can resume in Texas’s Big Bend sector while the case continues. Justice Jackson would have denied the government’s request.

items.notes: Bloomberg link paywalled. Relevant to W-261106-03 (checkDate Nov 12).
items.text: Trump said new strikes on Iran are "quite unlikely" though the US is "locked and loaded", and spoke of momentum toward ending the conflict. Iran’s foreign minister denied a reported Vance–Rezaei meeting in Qatar; Iranian officials say they won’t negotiate until the US meets their conditions. Brent fell to about $92.

Mississippi Senate: Democrat Scott Colom leads Sen. Hyde-Smith by 2,536 votes (49.1% to 48.8%) as the mail and affidavit-cure deadline passed; about 2,600 mail ballots were outstanding and 76% of 15,547 affidavit ballots processed were accepted. Counties must certify by Nov 13; the state has no automatic recount.

items.notes: Closes W-261105-05. Vote count and attendance not reported. President Święczkowski’s camp disputes the Assembly’s legality (check wPolityce).
items.text: A General Assembly of Constitutional Tribunal judges, called by Judge Korwin-Piotrowska, changed the Tribunal’s rules to curb the president’s solo powers: his budget report now needs the Assembly’s positive opinion. PM Tusk said the resolution would be published, and WP reports it has been.

The President’s chief of staff Bogucki said there are no conditions yet for a Nawrocki–Tusk meeting while police cordons stay at the Constitutional Tribunal and "legal" judges can’t enter. The PM’s office head Grabiec called these preconditions. The meeting expected around Nov 12 now looks unlikely.

The government adopted a bill amending the nuclear "special act": site decisions would no longer expire after 10 years, the investor would get land rights by law, some documents could be filed in English, and PEJ’s funding cap moves from 11bn to 8bn zł in 2026 and from 6.6bn to 9.6bn zł in 2030. It now goes to the Sejm.

items.thread: Poland public finances and credit ratings
items.text: PM Tusk said a government regulation will let more than 6bn zł from the EU’s SAFE defence loans go to the Police, Border Guard, State Fire Service and State Protection Service.

items.notes: Updates W-261108-05. No draft text yet.
items.text: After the Kraków attack, the Interior Ministry will review the 1999 Weapons and Ammunition Act; ideas include a register of black-powder guns and mandatory periodic checks of gun owners. Tusk asked ministers for an urgent review of rules on guns and shooting ranges.

New maximum fuel prices for Nov 11–12: petrol 95 at 6.10 zł/l, petrol 98 at 6.70 zł/l and diesel at 7.66 zł/l (petrol slightly up, diesel down from the Nov 10 caps). The Energy Minister wants to send a maximum gas price bill to parliament in November.

The Council of Ministers adopted a 2026–2028 regulatory programme to cut red tape for business (21 measures, per Manager Plus). The PIE business climate index fell 3.1 points to 99.3 in November; Q3 company bankruptcies were 108, up 7 year on year.
MPC member Gabriela Masłowska said the latest NBP projection justifies a rate hike in January, but suggested waiting until early next year when regulated prices are clearer.

items.notes: Another rp.pl headline gives 12 still in hospital.
items.text: The Małopolska voivode said 13 people injured in the attack were still in six Kraków hospitals on Tuesday morning, all stable; a woman and an Austrian man were discharged Monday. One of the two wounded police officers is conscious and recovering. President Nawrocki visited both officers and awarded them the Officer’s Cross of Polonia Restituta.

items.notes: Autopsy findings not yet published in sources read. Relevant to W-261110-02.
items.text: Police confirmed both officers who stopped the attacker wore body cameras, now secured; it is not yet known whether they recorded. Prosecutors are examining the attacker’s car, registered to his father, for a possible dashcam, and are reviewing city CCTV and amateur videos. Autopsies were carried out on Monday.

items.text: Independence Day in Kraków is scaled back because of the city mourning, which ends today: the patriotic march, picnic, service-vehicle parade, the singing session on the Main Square and the Patriotic Tram are cancelled, and the Independence Run is virtual. The 10:00 mass at Wawel Cathedral and the 12:00 ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on Plac Matejki go ahead.

items.notes: MoSPI press note: indiaeducationdiary.in republished it. Hindi coverage in Zee Business.
items.text: The official labour survey (PLFS) put unemployment for people aged 15+ at 5.1% in July–September, down from 5.4% in the previous quarter. Rural joblessness fell to 4.3% while urban unemployment edged up to 6.8%.

items.notes: Check LiveLaw / SC cause list for the order text.
items.text: In its suo motu case on "digital arrest" scams, the Supreme Court asked WhatsApp and other intermediaries to set out their anti-scam measures and send proposals to the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C). Next hearing: Nov 23.
The IMD expects a low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal around Nov 13 that could become a depression by Nov 15; its track and strength are not yet clear.
The second round of the Rs 37,500-crore coal gasification incentive scheme drew only two bids, both from NTPC (urea and methanol/DME). A third round opened Nov 10 with a Jan 11, 2027 deadline.
India and Oman began the 15th Naseem Al Bahr naval exercise off Oman (Nov 9–12); INS Surat is taking part.
Delhi’s first river cruise, the electric "Namo Yamuna River Safari" on the Sonia Vihar–Jagatpur stretch, launched under the Inland Waterways Authority and the Delhi government.
State decisions: Assam’s cabinet set aside Rs 200 crore for the Ayushman Asom health insurance scheme; Bihar raised dearness allowance for employees and pensioners from 60% to 63% from July 1.
